title: Grateful Dead Live at Eureka Municipal Auditorium on 1968-01-20

ai_review.summary: Excellent soundboard capture of a rare 1968 set featuring the jazzy Clementine suite, New Potato, Born Cross‑Eyed, Spanish Jam and more.
ai_review.review: The recording is a crystal‑clear soundboard source that lets every instrument shine, from Pigpen’s keyboard wizardry to Jerry’s spacious guitar tones. Musically the show is a pre‑1970 treasure – the first Clementine, the inaugural Spanish Jam, and seamless transitions into New Potato and Born Cross‑Eyed make it a must‑listen for Deadheads. Reviewers unanimously praise both the performance and the audio fidelity.

ai_rating.rationale: All five reviews are 5‑star, highlighting a superb rare performance and an excellent soundboard recording with no noted flaws.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Audio described as excellent and crystal‑clear; every instrument is audible with no reported dropouts or muddiness.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Rare first performances flow smoothly with seamless transitions; the jazzy suite feels sophisticated and the overall pacing is praised as one of the band’s best pre‑1970 shows.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Praised for spacious, deliberate guitar tone on New Potato and lead vocals on Clementine.
band_member_comments.Phil: Highlighted as co‑writer of Clementine; his influence from Coltrane is noted, and his bass work contributes to the jazzy feel.
band_member_comments.Keys: Pigpen on keyboards is described as being at his best, adding depth to the jams.
